values: Haven was founded by highly successful "privateers" nearly two centuries ago. Since then, as rival bands of pirates have fought over it, it has changed hands fourteen times, but has never been successfully invaded by the Republic. Numerous small manufacturing shops sell outfits that cannot be bought legally, and there is even a small shipyard where customized ships are sold to those who have the right connections.

Much of the planet is desert, but with enough moisture to grow enough crops to feed the entire population. Strip mining has turned other parts of the planet into barren wastelands, and has polluted many of the rivers.
The spaceport is old and dingy, with piles of litter in the gutters and graffiti on many of the alley walls. Many of the shops are closed, the windows boarded over or covered with yellowing paper.

This is an independent world, and a relatively stable settlement, but the effects of its separation from the rest of the galaxy are evident. A few young people carrying large backpacks eye you with interest, perhaps trying to gauge their chances of getting you to give them a cheap lift off-planet.

Around the back of the main yard, past the salvage lots, a handful of disc-shaped hulls sit under tarps. A dealer leans against one of them, arms crossed. "Corellian Engineering builds these on New Sahara. Officially, none of them end up here." He pulls back a tarp to reveal a sleek, modified hull. "The Vagabond's fast and quiet. The Privateer's for boarding work. And the Striker —" he grins "— the Striker's for people who think shields are a lifestyle and hull integrity is someone else's problem."

description.text: Scarlet is a sparsely populated farm world. The planet supplies food for the CSSF's soldiers and officials, to allow them to continue their war against the Sayari Plushie Authority. It is rumored that Scarlet is home to a secret weapons development lab and perhaps a large stockpile of nuclear weapons.

spaceport.text: Scarlet's spaceport consists of a large grid of landing. There are large fuel tanks and hangars nearby, alongside the stuff to be expected from a normal spaceport.

description.text: Laateli is an Earth-like planet home to a large shipyard and over 1.34 billion people. The streets of its largest city, Laadecki is bustling with small businesses strewn across the cityscape with the occasional chop-shop. The slave trade has proliferated deep within the planet's mantle. Amongst the inhabitants, there is rumor that deep in the nearby uninhabited systems lies an entrance to an alien civillization. No explorer has been daring enough to investigate this, and it is often dismissed as mere nonsense. Due to the large shipyards here, it is a popular stopping point for captains who wish to purchase new ships or upgrades.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is busy with ships docking and undocking constantly. Air traffic controllers continue to exist, but ever since spacecraft made atmospheric-based vehicles obsolete, their main responsibility is now to control the flow of ships into the system.

The planet is home to a large lumber industry, supplying lumber to most of human space to provide the Paradise Planets and anyone with the right amount of money with wooden furniture.

The planet is home to a large lumber industry, supplying lumber to most of human space to provide the Paradise Planets and anyone with the right amount of money with wooden furniture.

Merchant ships often stop by the area to purchase large amounts of lumber to sell to the Paradise Planets. Most of the dockworker's equipment seem to be specialized for carrying wood, and only wood. At least one section of the spaceport is made out of wood, from what you could discern when you landed.

description.text: Arlok is the home of the Sayari Plushie Authority's research facilities. Here, experimental technology of all kinds are experimented on and reverse-engineered. Outside the laboratories, the place is relatively pristine however there are plans to move most of the labs to somewhere else since SPA fleets have to cross through Republic space to get here.

spaceport.text: Arlok's spaceport is relatively large, with landing pads strewn across the surface of what seems to be a total land area of 1.32 square kilometers.

spaceport.text: Contrary to the other SPA planets, this one is relatively tame, with the ship traffic mostly composed of freighters and smaller ships. The escorts here are comprised of mostly smaller ships.

description.text: Eteristra is an undeveloped planet in the Pelitol Cluster. Eteristra acts primarily as a nature reserve.

spaceport.text: The spaceport here is primitive, with very few landing pads. Most traffic into the planet descends into the atmosphere to land in places far away from the spaceport, presumably to record the planet's wildlife (of which a sizable chunk was imported from Earth).

description.text: Perechra is an Earth-like world and the easternmost world in the Pelitol Cluster. With a population of 12,000, the world's facilities are primitive and meet only the barebones basic standards of medicine, hygiene and other critical services. Perechra is most often used as a rest stop for ships making their way to either Kaistra or Salistra.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is barebones, with just 5 landing pads for large ships. You see 4 small ships on one of the landing pads. People here give you weird looks, since not many people land often. Dental offices, shopping centers, and even a small hospital are visible from where you currently are.

description.text: This is an outpost. The station, located in the rings of Defal VI, is equipped with cannons on all sides to protect the station from asteroid impacts.

spaceport.text: Meanwhile, the spaceport village offers several services such as food, drinks, ship repairs, and most importantly, plushies of either Freya Winters or Sayari. The traffic at the spaceport is fairly light with a ship entering roughly every 4 minutes.

values: Barachen is an ocean world where roughly 85% of the surface is an ocean. Small settlements are present on most of Barachen's islands, home to a few plushie stashes and factories, most of which are well-hidden.
One of the larger island chains is home to a massive SPA naval base, the spaceport, and shipyard, presumably to intimidate the Republic outpost on Voreo.

spaceport.text: Voreo's spaceport is designed more for large ships. Soldiers and officers in Republic uniforms dominate the landscape, but thankfully are nice enough to refuel and repair your ship at no cost.

description.text: The Hidalgo Shrine, in orbit of Heine, is a planetwide museum of French history. The servers here have been continually running since 2871, surviving the war when the SPA split off from the Anime Organization.

spaceport.text: Nobody knows why it's called the Hidalgo Shrine.

values: The Hidalgo Shrine, in orbit of Heine, is a planetwide museum of French history. The servers here have been continually running since 2871, surviving the war when the SPA split off from the Anime Organization.

The walls of the spaceport appear as if thousands of images were once stuck to them, only having been recently removed. The station's docking ports are continually crowded with ships and tourists. Ships wanting to enter the station during peak hours sometimes wait in planetary orbit due to the unbearable traffic. The main spaceport building itself is a replica of the Hotel de Ville.

The nearby shops sell items related to France, such as baguettes, croissants, and other French items. The spaceport is the only settlement on this planet, home to roughly 11,000 people, the rest left barren and uninhabited. The signs are twice as large, as they have both English and French text.
Nobody knows why it's called the Hidalgo Shrine.

description.text: Heine is a planet of large farms and wheat fields. Over 80% of Heine's arable land is under the control of a single agricultural cooperative, known as the Heine Farming Federation. Unlike other planets where multiple cooperatives compete for domination over a planet's farmers, Heine's agricultural cooperative has dominated most of the planet. Other competing cooperatives were absorbed into the HFF or shut down a long time ago.

spaceport.text: As with many farming planets, the farmer's market is what uses up the vast majority of the spaceport's space and docking pads (for exports and imports). The only spaceport on Heine is under the control of the HFF, and they give priority to ships moving crops over ships carrying other types of cargo.

Today, Pondar is now home to 9,210 people and serves as a hotspot for pirate and CSSF activity. The CSSF and pirate warlords operate their own bases on Pondar.

spaceport.text: Pondar's spaceport is one of three ports on this planet. The other ports belong to the CSSF and pirate warlords respectively.

description.text: Moristra is the northernmost colony in the Pelitol Cluster. Moristra is primarily an agricultural colony with the exception of the spaceport city, where the farmer's market resides (it takes up over 75% of the spaceport city's space).

spaceport.text: Moristra's spaceport is home to the farmer's market, where farmers sell their crops and the occasional tractor salesman approaches you, and asks if you want one. Notably, Moristra has very strong right-to-repair laws for tractors and farm equipment, so there are countless facilities where farmers modify their equipment or watch as repairmen, experienced or not, repair their equipment.

spaceport.text: This spaceport is large; but the SPA military base is thrice as large. It is locked behind a tall electric fence and anti-ship turrets.

values: Bardanistra was first colonized by the Anime Organization in the 2720s. When the Sayari Plushie Authority split off from the Anime Organization, this colony stubbornly held on until the 2840s, even when they had lost military support from the A.O.
Today, most of the draconian measures implemented by the SPA such as martial law when they eventually gained full control are repealed; but a few of those measures still exist.

In the planet's orbit, there are a few hundred orbital turrets which are derelict and abandoned; leftovers from Bardanistra's resistance. They are not enough of a nuisance to the planet's orbital volume yet as to warrant a salvage operation.

Bardanistra's spaceport is located outside the main city. There are still several turrets left over from when the colony held out against the Sayari Plushie Authority, but some have already been upgraded to modern turrets. The security checkpoints, normally absent on other SPA planets, are still running, another leftover security measure from the old martial law era.

Near the spaceport lies a large SPA-owned military base, shipyard, and outfitter. The security is a bit more intense than the regular spaceport. The roof of the SPA-owned military base has significantly more turrets than the rest, which are of significantly higher quality.
This spaceport is large; but the SPA military base is thrice as large. It is locked behind a tall electric fence and anti-ship turrets.

spaceport.text: Your ship is refueled by the workers. Food is available at the spaceport for cheap.

description.text: The planet's surface consists of a single Pangaea-style continent. The northern hemisphere of the planet is home to the majority of the population; the landscape becoming more rural and less urbanized as one goes south. A medium-sized city surrounds the spaceport, which is unusual as the surrounding region is mostly barren and uninhabited.

spaceport.text: Near the spaceport, there is a large shopping center where all types of items can be bought. It is also a place where merchants and freight captains constantly haggle over the price of commodities. A large warehouse operated by the Sayari Plushie Authority takes up roughly one-third of the shopping center's space. As usual, it is used for plushie storage.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is located in one of the planet's valleys; the inhabitants of the spaceport village residing in a large network of caves. In one of the larger cave entrances near the spaceport, there is an outfitter and shipyard.

spaceport.text: Ancherum's spaceport and the main farmer's market are physically in the same building.

Naprai is primarily known for having a higher concentration of technology startups; the local government is sometimes forced to perform orbital cleanup operations in the rare chance that an experiment goes wrong either due to random chance or negligence.

spaceport.text: Naprai's spaceport is located outside of its largest city. Several large turrets are positioned outside the spaceport in the rare event that a piece of falling space debris from a failed experiment seems likely to hit the surface.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is connected to a large shopping center, where most of the commerce occurs.

values: Martieu is an unusually religious and conservative planet. Data chips on Martieu are frequently inspected and any chip containing "objectionable" material is destroyed. Aside from censorship of the galactic internet, the government of Martieu has implemented conservative policies.

description.text: Sparley is another Republic colony. Large settlements referred to as "favelas" (plural) dominate the vast majority of the landscape, except for the land near the spaceport, a few nature reserves, and the planet's large mountain ranges.

spaceport.text: The spaceport city is the only non-favela part of Sparley. The spaceport building is roughly octopus-shaped, with several landing pads for many different variants of ships near the spaceport's tentacle-like appendages.

values: The colony of Bredehoft, at the northeast of the Pelitol Cluster, is often nicknamed the law capital of the Cluster, due to its higher concentrations of lawyers compared to the other planets. It is sometimes said by the locals that a long bloodline of lawyers reside on this planet, going back to 21st century Earth.

Law firms have built several large buildings near the main spaceport, acting as their headquarters. The main planetary court of Bredehoft resides at the very periphery of the spaceport, consisting of several buildings and courtrooms, with a direct link to the spaceport and even landing pads of its own for particularly troublesome defendants, criminals, or plaintiffs.

spaceport.text: Pareia's spaceport is primitive. Not many ships land here on the very few landing pads available, which even then are simple concrete pads, instead of more advanced high-tech landing pads used on other worlds.

spaceport.text: The spaceport of Lattice contains many luxury stores, most of which are prohibitively expensive.

Tarsia is home to a large SPA distribution center, which is responsible for the sale and distribution of all plushies in the southeast Pelitol Cluster.

spaceport.text: Tarsia's spaceport is in a way, similar to Earth's spaceport. Serving a city of roughly 75 million people, most parts of the spaceport are dilapidated except for the private terminal reserved for the rich and famous. Some slave shops are likely operating within the deeper, more hidden parts of the spaceport.

description.text: Kabegan is home to the highest concentration of datacenters in the Pelitol Cluster. Data storage devices are some of the cheapest in the Pelitol Cluster, and has some of the strongest privacy laws in the Republic. Media may be assigned an age-appropriateness rating and censored on other worlds, but not on Kabegan, which has no rating system in place for all forms of media.

spaceport.text: There are dorms at the spaceport and a small village nearby. However, most of the settlement surrounding the spaceport is connected physically to the spaceport building itself. The dorms within the spaceport are likely reserved for the spaceport workers.

values: Unlike Martieu's notoriously high rates of religious adherence and strict data chip inspections and censorship laws, Kabegan is the opposite. Data chip inspections on Kabegan require search warrants, and over half of the planet's population is atheist. Several of Kabegan's settlements are located deep underground away from the planet's fault lines, some of which are barricaded by blast doors.

description.text: Laateli is an Earth-like planet home to a large shipyard and over 1.34 billion people. The streets of its largest city, Laadecki is bustling with small businesses strewn across the cityscape with the occasional chop-shop. The slave trade has proliferated deep within the planet's mantle. Amongst the inhabitants, there is rumor that deep in the nearby uninhabited systems lies an entrance to an alien civillization. No explorer has been daring enough to investigate this, and it is often dismissed as mere nonsense. Due to the large shipyards here, it is a popular stopping point for captains who wish to purchase new ships or upgrades.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is busy with ships docking and undocking constantly. Air traffic controllers continue to exist, but ever since spacecraft made atmospheric-based vehicles obsolete, their main responsibility is now to control the flow of ships into the system.

description.text: Denchrao is a large and urbanized world with several cities scattered over the many continent. Rather strangely, 55% of the planet is land, whereas the average proportion of land to water on other planets was far lower, somewhere between 30 to 40%. Outside of the cities, the nature is surprisingly pristine and is well-preserved and catalogued.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is located in the largest city on Denchrao. Businesspeople in suits can be seen conversing with SPA officers and carts full of plushies, either depicting Sayari, or Freya Winters.

description.text: This is a moon of the gas giant named Kestrix. Piracy runs rampant here on this world, and many pirates here have their guns pointed at you. Kestrix I is the most run-down of the three, where crews subservient to the inhabitants of Kestrix II and III live and toil. Arbitrary executions for even the smallest of mistakes are routine here, and no mercy is given.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is rundown and the conditions here are the worst of the other Kestrix moons. Food here is overpriced and sold by men who look like they're from either Kestrix II or III. Occasionally, one of the locals attempts to steal some food, but they are mercilessly executed. You decide to ignore all of this.

description.text: This is a moon of the gas giant named Kestrix. Piracy runs rampant here on this world, and many pirates here have their guns pointed at you. Kestrix III is the more populous planet of the three. None of the pirates here want to trade with you or sell you even the most basic of outfits. Most of the pirates here are big and rich pirate warlords while lower-class crew and captains reside on Kestrix I and II respectively. There are many crew here who normally would belong on Kestrix I or on Leroo Station. You do meet a few friendly merchant captains who want to trade.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is rundown and the conditions are almost inhuman. Well-dressed men (likely rich pirates) sit at their tables as poorer-looking men and women bring them plates full of food. There is a field hospital here, but it is relatively empty, and it is likely the only medical care facility in the Kestrix Moons.

description.text: Eisei is the home of the Anime Organization, the predecessor state to the Sayari Plushie Authority. Their mandate has always been the preservation of anime. Anime screenings occur often on this world. As for the planet itself, the land-to-water ratio is similar to Earth, with a large desert covering 43% of the main continent. The coastline is heavily urbanized, and it appears the Anime Organization calls the shots on this world, with little interference from the Republic or Free Worlds.

spaceport.text: The main spaceport is large. Advertisements for anime screenings litter the walls, while bookstores tout their 'new mangas' in stock. This is as 'Japanese' as the spaceport can get. Flags which look like red circles on white backgrounds adorn some of these bookstores.

values: The Sayari Ring is a partial ringworld, set to be the future new capital of the SPA, which will replace Khoramelia once it is complete. Despite being under-construction, the amenities are shockingly complete and the station bustling with human settlement and the occasional forklift carrying boxes of plushies in clear containers.
Massive thrusters have been mounted on the ring, to prevent its orbit from destabilizing.

The ring is wide. Due to its immense size, there are multiple spaceports scattered across the ring. You are in one of the larger ones. A massive SPA department store is at the exit of the spaceports, easily accessible, with tall shelves of plushie boxes in the industrial-looking storage area, being tended to by fast-moving machinery either depositing or taking products.
Most of the industrial storage area is separated from the spaceport hallways by thick glass. It appears that the Authority is proud of this particular storage system.

description.text: Anna's World (formally known as Aixafer VIII) is a gas giant. The planet got its name when Anna Fangvin, an author whose books saw moderate success on nearby Denchrao, revealed that she repeatedly traveled here to seek inspiration for her book, 'Beyond the Hyperdrive'. A small station exists in orbit, selling Fangvin's books, without providing basic spaceport services.

Sometimes, Lethmith is used as a starting point to launch remains into interstellar space.

Notably, Moristra has very strong right-to-repair laws for tractors and farm equipment, so there are countless facilities where farmers modify their equipment or watch as repairmen, experienced or not, repair their equipment.

description.text: The planet's surface consists of a single Pangaea-style continent. The northern hemisphere of the planet is home to the majority of the population; the landscape becoming more rural and less urbanized as one goes south. A medium-sized city surrounds the spaceport, which is unusual as the surrounding region is mostly barren and uninhabited.

spaceport.text: Near the spaceport, there is a large shopping center where all types of items can be bought. It is also a place where merchants and freight captains constantly haggle over the price of commodities. A large warehouse operated by the Sayari Plushie Authority takes up roughly one-third of the shopping center's space. As usual, it is used for plushie storage.

values: Ondoristra was first colonized by the Anime Organization in the 2740s. When the Sayari Plushie Authority split off from the Anime Organization, Ondoristra was ceded over after the end of a brutal 3-year-long civil war. However, these days, the A.O and the SPA are on peaceful terms.

values: Bardanistra was first colonized by the Anime Organization in the 2720s. When the Sayari Plushie Authority split off from the Anime Organization, this colony stubbornly held on until the 2840s, even when they had lost military support from the A.O.
Today, most of the draconian measures implemented by the SPA such as martial law when they eventually gained full control are repealed; but a few of those measures still exist.

In the planet's orbit, there are a few hundred orbital turrets which are derelict and abandoned; leftovers from Bardanistra's resistance. They are not enough of a nuisance to the planet's orbital volume yet as to warrant a salvage operation.

Bardanistra's spaceport is located outside the main city. There are still several turrets left over from when the colony held out against the Sayari Plushie Authority, but some have already been upgraded to modern turrets. The security checkpoints, normally absent on other SPA planets, are still running, another leftover security measure from the old martial law era.

Near the spaceport lies a large SPA-owned military base, shipyard, and outfitter. The security is a bit more intense than the regular spaceport. The roof of the SPA-owned military base has significantly more turrets than the rest, which are of significantly higher quality.
This spaceport is large; but the SPA military base is thrice as large. It is locked behind a tall electric fence and anti-ship turrets.

description.text: Perechra is an Earth-like world and the easternmost world in the Pelitol Cluster. With a population of 12,000, the world's facilities are primitive and meet only the barebones basic standards of medicine, hygiene and other critical services. Perechra is most often used as a rest stop for ships making their way to either Kaistra or Salistra.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is barebones, with just 5 landing pads for large ships. You see 4 small ships on one of the landing pads. People here give you weird looks, since not many people land often. Dental offices, shopping centers, and even a small hospital are visible from where you currently are.

The colony of Kaistra in the neighboring Sarut system is the Salistra Shipyard's primary source of material.

spaceport.text: The Salistra Spaceport is located on an island in the middle of one of Salistra's large oceans.

Naprai is primarily known for having a higher concentration of technology startups; the local government is sometimes forced to perform orbital cleanup operations in the rare chance that an experiment goes wrong either due to random chance or negligence.

spaceport.text: Naprai's spaceport is located outside of its largest city. Several large turrets are positioned outside the spaceport in the rare event that a piece of falling space debris from a failed experiment seems likely to hit the surface.

description.text: Heine is a planet of large farms and wheat fields. Over 80% of Heine's arable land is under the control of a single agricultural cooperative, known as the Heine Farming Federation. Unlike other planets where multiple cooperatives compete for domination over a planet's farmers, Heine's agricultural cooperative has dominated most of the planet. Other competing cooperatives were absorbed into the HFF or shut down a long time ago.

spaceport.text: As with many farming planets, the farmer's market is what uses up the vast majority of the spaceport's space and docking pads (for exports and imports). The only spaceport on Heine is under the control of the HFF, and they give priority to ships moving crops over ships carrying other types of cargo.

description.text: The Hidalgo Shrine, in orbit of Heine, is a planetwide museum of French history. The servers here have been continually running since 2871, surviving the war when the SPA split off from the Anime Organization.

spaceport.text: Nobody knows why it's called the Hidalgo Shrine.

values: The Hidalgo Shrine, in orbit of Heine, is a planetwide museum of French history. The servers here have been continually running since 2871, surviving the war when the SPA split off from the Anime Organization.

The walls of the spaceport appear as if thousands of images were once stuck to them, only having been recently removed. The station's docking ports are continually crowded with ships and tourists. Ships wanting to enter the station during peak hours sometimes wait in planetary orbit due to the unbearable traffic. The main spaceport building itself is a replica of the Hotel de Ville.

The nearby shops sell items related to France, such as baguettes, croissants, and other French items. The spaceport is the only settlement on this planet, home to roughly 11,000 people, the rest left barren and uninhabited. The signs are twice as large, as they have both English and French text.
Nobody knows why it's called the Hidalgo Shrine.

description.text: Sparley is another Republic colony. Large settlements referred to as "favelas" (plural) dominate the vast majority of the landscape, except for the land near the spaceport, a few nature reserves, and the planet's large mountain ranges.

spaceport.text: The spaceport city is the only non-favela part of Sparley. The spaceport building is roughly octopus-shaped, with several landing pads for many different variants of ships near the spaceport's tentacle-like appendages.

description.text: Mirdenheim is a heavily urbanized colony bordering the SPA colony of Defal, with a population of roughly 898 million. Mirdenheim is one of the major colonies in the Pelitol Cluster and is home to a major Navy base and a forward operating base for conducting surveillance on the nearby Sayari Plushie Authority colonies.

spaceport.text: Mirdenheim's spaceport is at the outskirts of the largest city on Mirdenheim, and is right next to the shipyard. Large turrets are placed on the shipyard and spaceport buildings to guard against pirate attacks.

description.text: 60% of the surface of Martieu is an ocean. The remaining 40% has been subject to urbanization and deforestation.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is connected to a large shopping center, where most of the commerce occurs.

values: Martieu is an unusually religious and conservative planet. Data chips on Martieu are frequently inspected and any chip containing "objectionable" material is destroyed. Aside from censorship of the galactic internet, the government of Martieu has implemented conservative policies.
60% of the surface of Martieu is an ocean. The remaining 40% has been subject to urbanization and deforestation.

Martieu's spaceport is located at the largest city. Security guards can be seen inspecting people's data chips for so-called "objectionable" material. The spaceport has several different types of bays, optimized for loading and unloading either passengers or several types of cargo.
The spaceport is connected to a large shopping center, where most of the commerce occurs.

description.text: Kabegan is home to the highest concentration of datacenters in the Pelitol Cluster. Data storage devices are some of the cheapest in the Pelitol Cluster, and has some of the strongest privacy laws in the Republic. Media may be assigned an age-appropriateness rating and censored on other worlds, but not on Kabegan, which has no rating system in place for all forms of media.

spaceport.text: There are dorms at the spaceport and a small village nearby. However, most of the settlement surrounding the spaceport is connected physically to the spaceport building itself. The dorms within the spaceport are likely reserved for the spaceport workers.

values: Unlike Martieu's notoriously high rates of religious adherence and strict data chip inspections and censorship laws, Kabegan is the opposite. Data chip inspections on Kabegan require search warrants, and over half of the planet's population is atheist. Several of Kabegan's settlements are located deep underground away from the planet's fault lines, some of which are barricaded by blast doors.

Kabegan is home to the highest concentration of datacenters in the Pelitol Cluster. Data storage devices are some of the cheapest in the Pelitol Cluster, and has some of the strongest privacy laws in the Republic. Media may be assigned an age-appropriateness rating and censored on other worlds, but not on Kabegan, which has no rating system in place for all forms of media.

Kabegan's spaceport is located in one of the most mountainous parts of the planet, with several atmospheric routes extending out from the spaceport towards the most populated cities. Pastors and proselytizers roam the spaceport at times attempting to convert the planet's atheist population, but are simply ignored, treated as if they were never there.

There are dorms at the spaceport and a small village nearby. However, most of the settlement surrounding the spaceport is connected physically to the spaceport building itself. The dorms within the spaceport are likely reserved for the spaceport workers.

description.text: Tarsia is another one of the developed and heavily urbanized planets of the southeast parts of the Pelitol Cluster. Tarsia is home to a significant SPA presence, though not enough for this planet to be governed outright by them. Tarsia is home to a large SPA distribution center, which is responsible for the sale and distribution of all plushies in the southeast Pelitol Cluster.

spaceport.text: Tarsia's spaceport is in a way, similar to Earth's spaceport. Serving a city of roughly 75 million people, most parts of the spaceport are dilapidated except for the private terminal reserved for the rich and famous. Some slave shops are likely operating within the deeper, more hidden parts of the spaceport.

description.text: The forest surrounding the city is home to several native species of trees. It is for this reason that ships are inspected closely for the presence of any invasive species.

spaceport.text: The spaceport on Taraz is located in a small exclave surrounded by the nature reserve. From space, a line of deforested land can be seen running between the spaceport and the Taraz metropolitan area. This strip of land is the only major route and is high traffic with a large team of air traffic controllers coordinating spaceship traffic along the route.

values: Taraz is a forest world. The vast majority of the population of Taraz reside in a single metropolitan area. Over 75% of the land on Taraz has been designated as a nature reserve, and only biologists, scientists reside on that part of the planet. Not to be confused with Tarsia in the neighboring Vachrau system or Tarazed.

description.text: The culture of Gura is mostly influenced by Japanese culture. Gura is a colony of hundreds of millions.

spaceport.text: Gura has several spaceports scattered along the equator in place of a single large spaceport. Several industrial complexes on the surface have their own spaceport facilities.

description.text: Pareia is a large planetwide nature reserve. Most of the planet's species are imported from Earth. Small groups of Amish reside on this relatively undeveloped planet in the areas open to settlement.

spaceport.text: Pareia's spaceport is primitive. Not many ships land here on the very few landing pads available, which even then are simple concrete pads, instead of more advanced high-tech landing pads used on other worlds.

description.text: Steirek is a militarized world. It is for the exclusive use of the Sayari Plushie Authority. Steirek consists of a large network of warehouses, datacenters, and supercomputers providing storage for plushies and data and computing power to help the SPA choose the best place to sell plushies based on its models of the galaxy, which rival that of the Syndicate.

spaceport.text: The vast majority of the ships leaving and entering the spaceport are in the livery of the Sayari Plushie Authority and your ship sticks out amongst the crowd. Containers full of plushies can be seen being loaded onto the ships. The spaceport is defended by hundreds of turrets to protect against CSSF and pirate intrusions.

spaceport.text: Ponarai's spaceport is fairly primitive; some ships can even be seen directly on the ground; without a landing pad.

description.text: Narchrai's population density is unusually high. Untouched grasslands and forests still cover over 90% of the surface, the remaining 10% being a single continuous metropolitan area home to large buildings. Collectively, these large buildings host roughly hundreds of millions of people.

spaceport.text: Narchrai's primary spaceport is located atop the city's tallest building. The immense size of the spaceport shrouds the nearby buildings into darkness for a few kilometers extending out from the center.

description.text: Pechara High is sparsely populated. Only roughly 40 people live here to maintain the station and perform research. It orbits the gas giant Pechara, which was expelled from its star system likely hundreds of millions of years ago. An even bigger mystery is why the hyperlane network would lead to such an isolated and lonely gas giant.

spaceport.text: The spaceport consists primarily of equipment for launching scientific probes alongside standard refuelling facilities.

description.text: The Brigantium Computing Array, while primarily used for scientific research, has had a part of its computing power rented out for a variety of purposes such as rendering of extremely high-quality images and movies, simulation of galactic trade prices and combat simulations. Over 99.8% of Brigantium's permanent population consist of people who maintain the Array alongside their families and close relatives.

spaceport.text: Many PC shops here sell parts taken from decommissioned Array servers, alongside prebuilt machines using the very same parts.

values: Brigantium is home to the Brigantium Computing Array: a network of supercomputers across the surface, capable of running highly intensive simulations, using the water as a heatsink. The Array is powered by a partial Dyson sphere, the sole source of power in the Brigantium system.

The Brigantium Computing Array, while primarily used for scientific research, has had a part of its computing power rented out for a variety of purposes such as rendering of extremely high-quality images and movies, simulation of galactic trade prices and combat simulations. Over 99.8% of Brigantium's permanent population consist of people who maintain the Array alongside their families and close relatives.

The spaceport on Brigantium is located on top of one of the array's largest nodes. There is a relatively high demand for electronics to replace some of the failing parts of the Array, and data-chips containing high quality images, rendered by the array at extremely high resolutions, so high that even at 500x zoom level the image was still 4K.
Many PC shops here sell parts taken from decommissioned Array servers, alongside prebuilt machines using the very same parts.

description.text: Lattice is primarily an upscale colony, with the vast majority of the population being either rich or retired. Most of the planet's poorer population originate from the other parts of the Pelitol cluster; it is essentially an enclave of the Paradise Worlds.

spaceport.text: The spaceport of Lattice contains many luxury stores, most of which are prohibitively expensive.

values: Lattice is primarily an upscale colony, with the vast majority of the population being either rich or retired. Most of the planet's poorer population originate from the other parts of the Pelitol cluster; it is essentially an enclave of the Paradise Worlds.

description.text: Bredehoft is an Earth-like planet with a roughly 1:1 ratio of land and water.

spaceport.text: Aside from the court, the spaceport is closely integrated with the planet's largest city, home to roughly 30% of the population.

values: The colony of Bredehoft, at the northeast of the Pelitol Cluster, is often nicknamed the law capital of the Cluster, due to its higher concentrations of lawyers compared to the other planets. It is sometimes said by the locals that a long bloodline of lawyers reside on this planet, going back to 21st century Earth.
Bredehoft is an Earth-like planet with a roughly 1:1 ratio of land and water.

Law firms have built several large buildings near the main spaceport, acting as their headquarters. The main planetary court of Bredehoft resides at the very periphery of the spaceport, consisting of several buildings and courtrooms, with a direct link to the spaceport and even landing pads of its own for particularly troublesome defendants, criminals, or plaintiffs.
Aside from the court, the spaceport is closely integrated with the planet's largest city, home to roughly 30% of the population.

description.text: Couric is a Pirate world, used as a rallying point for attacks against the Republic or the Sayari Plushie Authority to the west. The vast majority of Couric is controlled by a single syndicate. First landed on by a local pirate warlord known as Raugan in 2994 in an attempt to evade pursuit.

spaceport.text: Couric has no single spaceport; spaceports are spread out across the planet for redundancy in the event of a hostile planetary attack.

missions.description: Transport <tons> of <commodity> to <planet>, <system>, to assist the Anime Organization in further expanding their collection of anime. You will be paid <payment> for this.

values: Transport <tons> of <commodity> to <planet>, <system>, to assist the Anime Organization in further expanding their collection of anime. You will be paid <payment> for this.
You still don't have the anime. Please come back when you have it.

children.key: As you walk through the Anime Organization spaceport, pondering your next move, a man in a brown uniform approaches you. Reading from his clipboard, he flips through the pages before looking up to face you.
"Greetings. Would you be willing to do the Anime Organization a favor?"

"We recently purchased data drives containing some extremely rare anime from a private collector. Sadly, for the past few days, we have been unable to arrange for a captain to transport the anime, as all our ships were currently unavailable for courier jobs. Until we found you. We would like you to pick up the drives on <stopovers> and bring them back here to <origin>.

"The private collector will be waiting for you on Alexandria, in the visitor center. Scan through all the tables until you find them. You will be paid <payment> for this once we confirm that the anime is directly within our possession," explains the worker.
"Sorry, but I'm not going all the way to <stopovers>."
The worker, enraged that you have insulted anime, pulls out their gun and terminates you.

You leave your ship, opening the hatch. You recall that the worker had informed you that the private collector would be in the visitor center. So, you begin marching across the docking bays of Alexandria, eventually arriving in the spaceport's visitor center, after a short brisk walk.

As you scan the room in search for the mysterious collector, you spot a middle-aged woman dressed in a white pantsuit waving at you, the buttons on her suit jacket's sleeves occasionally visible, reflecting light into your eyes. She must be the private collector. You approach her table and take a seat on the other side.
"Are you the captain the Anime Organization sent to pick up the anime?", asks the lady.
"Yes, they sent me here.", you reply.
"I'll have the dockworkers load the anime onto your ship. After this, you are to return to <planet>."

You stand up to return to your ship, the woman following at the same pace as you. By the time you arrive, dockworkers have already opened your ship's hatch, with large crates of anime being loaded. Once all is done, you board your ship, wish the woman well, and prepare to transport the anime back to <planet>.

As your ship begins deorbiting, you receive a special message from Eisei Control, directing you to land on a separate hangar. As you exit the hatch, the same Anime Organization worker walks in with his clipboard. Once he approaches close enough, he extends a credit chip with <payment> from his uniform's pocket and gives it to you.

"I'll have the dock workers unload the anime from your ship very soon. Be patient. Anyways, thank you for your contribution to anime history. Your efforts are not in vain. The anime that you have transported will be lovingly preserved by our archivists. I wish you the best in your future endeavors.

You sit back as the dockworkers begin unloading the cargo, with a great deal of care so as to not damage the data drives. After what seems like a few hours of painstakingly careful unloading, the hangar door opens and you return to the primary spaceport, leaving you to ponder your next move.

missions.name: CVH sales pitch 1

values: A property agent based on Asgard, Naos. She runs her own property agency. You have had multiple run-ins with her, whether it was her boarding your ship, her approaching you, or selling you an apartment.

children.key: When you land on <origin> and open your hatch, a woman in a well-pressed green pantsuit rushes in, sitting on a nearby table.
"Get out of my ship right now!"
You walk over to the table where she is sitting at.
The unknown woman in the green pantsuit takes something from her pocket and hands it to you. It is yet another card. Her name, 'Carla von Hausen', is written on it.
"Hello!" She smiles at you. "<origin> is a really great place, isn't it? Have you reconsidered your decision to purchase a home?"
"I'm curious. Do you want to explain to me why I should get a home on Asgard?"

The unknown woman in the green pantsuit hands you her name card and leaves your ship. Her name was 'Carla von Hausen'. You vaguely remember that when you were here earlier, she had approached you wanting to sell you a house.

After realizing you are serious, Carla leaves behind her card and the advertising materials on the table. She picks up her other items, double-checking to ensure she didn't forget anything, smoothing and adjusting her suit jacket on the way out. Eventually, she leaves your ship.
You immediately close the hatch and lock the door. Being suddenly interrupted, you have now forgotten what you were supposed to do. You read over your checklist to see what it must have been.
"Well, that's fair. But remember, there's so much to see on Asgard. If you ever reconsider in the future, just send mail to the address on the name card."

Carla leaves behind her card and the advertising materials on the table. She picks up her other items, double-checking to ensure she didn't forget anything, smoothing and adjusting her suit jacket on the way out.

Carla lays out some advertising materials, before going into a puffery-laden speech about the state of the housing market and the 'great and rich' culture on <origin>, the nearby restaurants, swimming pools, libraries and other amenities, the great experiences, and the prestigious universities and schools nearby.

Sometimes, her speech is so fast that it is nearly incomprehensible. She gestures wildly, to the point where the buttons on her suit jacket's sleeve are briefly visible, and at some points nearly slapping you, only dodging mere milliseconds before impact.
After roughly 8 minutes of continuing to listen to her speech, you eventually begin to have an annoyed look on your face.

"Your home may be the stars and your ship, but you can't live here forever. You will eventually need a world to call home. The secret of Helsingor is about to leak, and once it does, the prices will climb! You're in on a rare opportunity to see how great Asgard is before the rest!"
"I'm not convinced. Can you please leave now?"
"Sorry, I'm still not interested in buying a house."
"Great!", says Carla. "I have an opening today, so we can check out the house and see if it is right for you."
"Where is the house, exactly?", you ask.
"Just outside the city center. It's an apartment.", Carla replies. "It should be a 20-minute bus ride from here."

Carla gets up from her seat, smoothing and adjusting her suit jacket as necessary and fastening a few buttons. She collects her things. After a few minutes you open the hatch and begin walking to the nearest bus stop.

After a few minutes of both of you sitting, the bus arrives. You and Carla get on the bus, finding a seat in the front. You both pay the fare. Occasionally, to pass the time and stave off boredom, she tells you one of her many stories about life as a property agent, such as the time she accidentally stepped over a child's toy set, the time she found magazines of a certain type on the desk, and the occasional renter who acted rude towards a client during a showing.

Once the stop is in sight Carla approaches the door, and you follow. The door opens, and you walk for a few minutes, enter an elevator, and arrive on the 18th floor. She brings out a ring of keys and browses through them to find the proper key and eventually opens the door.

You enter the apartment. It only has a bed, table, a sofa, and a few chairs. The apartment contains a single bedroom, a bathroom, and a large living room, alongside a small storage room between the kitchen and the living room.

Carla begins explaining. Unlike the speech she gave at the table on your ship, this time she speaks in a clear voice. "It's a one-bedroom apartment. The bedroom should be large enough for three people. If you want to rent, it is 5,800 credits per month, and if you want to buy it, it should cost about 810,000 credits. The purchase price includes the furniture."
"So, what will it be?", she asks.

The professional smile on Carla's face asserts itself even stronger. "Good. I will say it again. The house costs 810,000 credits. Once I receive your payment, I will hand you the key, and from there on, the house will be yours. Your main home may be the stars and outer space, but when you retire, you'll have this house. You can even have it for your family."

She hands you a clipboard with the purchase agreement. You sit down on the table while you read the contract. Carla disappears into the bedroom. While you review the terms, you can sometimes hear her taking some calls in the distance.

You begin to speak with a slightly raised voice. "Carla, I've read the contract and I've made my decision. Please come here." Carla excuses herself from the phone and walks up to the table, taking a seat.
"Sorry, but I've changed my mind. I don't want the apartment."
"You made the right decision today.", says Carla in a happy tone. She watches as you bring out your pen and sign with your...
"Wait, you're left-handed too? I'm actually left-handed myself!", comments Carla as you sign your name.

With the ink of your signature now dried on the paper, you hand Carla a credit chip with 810,000 credits. She then reaches into her bag, retrieves a keyring, removes several keys from it, puts them on another smaller keyring, and hands them to you. She explains to you what door each individual key is for.

You shake hands with the agent, and wish each other well. You are now in your brand new house. Carla again smooths and adjusts her suit jacket, fastening a few buttons once more before she walks off. You lock the door behind her and begin contemplating on what to do with your new house.
Eventually, you decide to leave. You board a bus to the spaceport, and return to your ship.

As you speak those few words, Carla's smile temporarily gives way to a frown and maybe even an angry face. You greet each other farewell, and you leave the house. As you exit the front door, she locks the door behind you. You board a bus to the spaceport and return to your ship.

children.key: As you walk to the spaceport, a woman approaches you.
I have a job for you. I'm moving to <destination> soon. I just want a captain who will transport me and my stuff. It should be roughly <tons>.
"Sorry, I'm not headed there right now."
"How much are you willing to pay me?"
"I can pay you <payment>.", explains the woman.
"Okay, I will be willing to transport you."
"Sorry, but I can't take a job for that amount of money."

"Great!", says the woman. "I'll load my cargo onto your ship.". A few dockworkers arrive and begin loading what looks like her items into the hatch. With the items loaded, you show the woman her bunk as you go to the bridge. "Oh, and the name's Elaine".
Your ship enters the atmosphere of Asgard. As you land on the spaceport and prepare to open the hatch, you approach the woman..
"So by any chance, who's your landlord?"
"Her name is 'Carla von Hausen'. I'm renting.", says Elaine.

A truck pulls in, stopping near your ship. As the hatch opens, a few dockworkers enter and begin lifting furniture and carrying smaller items outside of the ship into the truck. Just as you and Elaine leave the ship, a woman in a red pantsuit approaches.
As she approaches you, she identifies herself as 'Carla von Hausen'.
"Thank you very much, Captain <last>. I appreciate your help in getting my tenant and her stuff transported to Asgard.
For the next half-hour, Carla and Elaine observe as the dockworkers continue loading the truck. Just as the last of the cargo is loaded, you hear a taxi stop nearby.
"Sure, I'd love to go with you."
"No, I'm going on my own now."

The three of you board the taxi. The truck begins departing the spaceport, while the taxi follows. Eventually, you arrive at your destination. The three of you then leave the taxi. A van that you haven't noticed stops nearby. A group of workers begin unloading Elaine's items from the truck, while another group lays down protective covers on the walls, floor, and elevator interior.
"Greetings to all residents! A new tenant is moving into your block. We apologize for the noise and inconvenience.", says one of the workers over the apartment block's PA system.
Elaine then approaches you, and hands you a credit chip containing <payment>. You wave goodbye to Carla and Elaine as they disappear into one of the elevators.
"Are you going to return to the spaceport <first>? I have to go back to the city soon!", yells the taxi driver.

"Yes! I'm going back.", you reply, in a voice matching that of the driver. You walk back to the taxi, open the door, and put on your seatbelt. Eventually, you arrive at the spaceport and return to your ship, ready to leave.

missions.name: Person ranting about date format

children.key: As you walk through the spaceport, a person approaches you.
"Hey Captain, I'm having trouble reading this date. Can you help me?"
You approach the person and read the date that has been displayed. It says '04/07/3027'.
"It could also be the 4th of July", says the person.
"It could also be April 7th", says the person.
After a slight pause of a few seconds, the person pulls out a loudspeaker and begins speaking through it, broadcasting their opinions about the date format for the whole spaceport to hear.

"It's all so confusing! At least spell out the date or use year-month-day! But seriously, year-month-day is so much better because it's just so logical! It goes largest to smallest, it's still logical when you add the time to it, and it's been an international standard for so long!", rants the person.

They continue their rant. "It's always clear, and if everybody was using it we wouldn't have to be so confused about whether a date like 04/07 is April 7th or the 4th of July! I've already sent so many emails to shipyards everywhere requesting they change their date format to year-month-day and they all keep saying no!"
"Year-month-day is the way to keep our society running without the evils of unclear date formats! Down with all other formats!"
"But make sure to write only 4-digit years and never 2-digit years because then it's just much worse! 22-12-14 is a terrible date format! Is it 3022-12-14, or is it 3014-12-22? It's so confusing!"

"If you have a computer, you should always use year-month-day for your computer files because they sort well! No need to sort by filesystem date, because it just sorts well! No special code to parse the date is needed!"
"It's also consistent with the way we write numbers! Consistent with the Hindu-Arabic numeral system we all use! Largest to smallest!"

children.key: As you walk through the spaceport, you overhear an argument between a captain and a bunch of dockworkers.
"No, this cargo was loaded on December 4th, not April 12th!", says the captain in an angry voice, holding a clipboard of some sort.
"Sir, the clipboard uses day-month-year, not month-day-year.", replies the dockworker, in a calm tone.
After your interjection, both parties look at you. "I guess we can do that.", says the dockworker. "Year-month-day is better anyway.".
The dockworker takes a new clipboard and starts redoing the paperwork, this time in year-month-day format.
